label: ACSC Essential Eight
coverage_note: ACSC publishes eight named mitigation strategies, not numbered controls, so control_id below is a stable slug of the strategy name rather than an invented identifier. Only 'Patch Operating Systems' and 'Restrict Administrative Privileges' have any host-level, network-facing signal this tool can observe -- and only partially even then (e.g. 'Patch Operating Systems' here means only 'the OS reported a successful update install timestamp', not patch currency against a specific CVE or SLA target, and says nothing about maturity level). The other six strategies -- Patch Applications, Multi-factor Authentication, Application Control, Restrict Microsoft Office Macro Settings, User Application Hardening, Regular Backups -- are completely outside what a single host's network-facing configuration audit can see. They are listed with no mapped checks and are always not_assessed here; that is a statement about this tool's vantage point, not a finding that they are failing.
